# Club boat bookings

A member books one of the club's boats for a morning or an afternoon. Only a member who has done the
checkout for that type of boat may book it. The bosun takes a boat out of service when it needs work, and
nobody can book it until it is back.

## What it must do

- A member sees every boat for a day, with each half day free or taken.
- A member who has not done the checkout for a boat's type sees that boat greyed, with *Not checked out on
  keelboats. Ask the training officer.* The boats are shown, not hidden, so a member sees what they could
  sail after a checkout.
- Booking a free half day confirms at once and appears under *My bookings*.
- A member cancels their own booking from *My bookings*, up to the start of the half day.
- The bosun takes a boat out of service with a date and a reason; a member sees it greyed with the date
  and who set it.
- A member who has no bookings is told so at the top of *Book a boat*, with the boats still shown
  beneath, so the page does not look broken.

## How to tell it works

- Sam, a member checked out on dinghies, books Kestrel for Saturday morning and sees it under *My bookings*.
- Sam taps Sandpiper, a keelboat, and is told to ask the training officer; nothing is booked.
- Jo, the bosun, takes Sandpiper out of service; Sam then sees Sandpiper greyed with the date and Jo's name.
- Sam cancels the Kestrel booking and the morning is free for everyone again.

## Out of scope

- Payment of any kind. Boat use is covered by membership.
- Recording a checkout. It is recorded on paper in the clubhouse and stays there for now.
- Offline use. The product is used on the clubhouse wifi.

## Who runs it

- Used by: staff — the club's members and its bosun, all named
- When it is down: an annoyance — bookings go back to the whiteboard for an afternoon

## Open

- Can a member hold two bookings on the same day?
